title: Microsoft says ‘people matter more than AI’ following safety concerns
slides: Microsoft claims people matter more than AI—so why the safety fears?
After incidents, Microsoft reaffirms human oversight in AI systems.
But internal memos reveal AI often bypasses human judgment under pressure.
If you use Microsoft AI, demand audit logs and human override options.
Ask: does your AI have a kill switch? Test it today.
thread_text:
1. Human Oversight or Window Dressing?

Microsoft says people matter more than AI. After a series of incidents, they reaffirmed human oversight. But what does that actually mean in practice?

2. The Pressure Valve Problem

Internal memos reveal AI often bypasses human judgment when deadlines loom. Under pressure, the override becomes a rubber stamp, not a safeguard.

3. Your Access to the Black Box

If you use Microsoft AI, you have a right to demand audit logs and a real human override option. Most users never ask. That's how systems drift.

4. The Kill Switch Question

Does your AI have a kill switch? If you don't know, you're not in control. Test it today on a non-critical task before you need it for real.

5. Test It Before You Trust It

Take one AI tool you rely on. Try to override its output manually. If you can't, ask your vendor why. Do it this week, not after the next incident.
